text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High rate of allocator failures and latency cliffs on runtime-pool-us-east-1 — affected route: /v1/embeddings (customers: subset of A/B test). Error spike started ~3788879940. Correlation: KV cache growth + continuous-batching surge. https://internal/alerts/3788880000

maria: seeing lots of `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation` in the pod logs, and torch malloc logs show repeated arena alloc attempts then small frees. percentile latency for embeddings jumped 4x.

ankit: confirmed — metrics show prefix_cache_bytes on runtime-hosts up 6x vs baseline, and continuous_batching inflight batches jumped after the 03:10 deploy.

jess: @oncall (me) taking. quick question — is this across regions or isolated?

kevin: mostly us-east-1 (10 hosts). ap-northeast minimal. looks like a config flip on the batcher: `max_batch_tokens` bumped to 16384 by a rollout earlier. that interacts poorly with kv slab allocator fragmentation.

samir: logs from one host:
```
2026-03-15T03:12:02Z runtime[pid=2222] WARN alloc: arena->reslice failed, slab_gap=0x1f6, requested=0x4000
2026-03-15T03:12:02Z runtime[pid=2222] ERROR cuda: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
2026-03-15T03:12:03Z runtime[pid=2222] INFO kvcache: inserting prefix 132k -> cache_size 12.1GB
```

maria: that slab_gap line is the allocator failing to coalesce small free segments — fragmentation ramping. combined with huge batch token targets, KV growth does many small allocations which never line up.

ankit: immediate mitigations we can do: 1) rollback the batcher change (reduce `max_batch_tokens` to 4096 or earlier value), 2) temporarily disable continuous batching on embeddings route, 3) trigger arena compaction on hot hosts.

jess: actioning rollback + disable on canary first. can someone run the rollback command?

kevin: running rollback on canary now:
```
# rollback batcher config on canary runtime group
redwoodctl cfg set runtime/continuous_batching.max_batch_tokens=4096 --group=canary
redwoodctl cfg set runtime/continuous_batching.enabled=false --route=/v1/embeddings --group=canary
```

kevin: done on canary, tailing logs. latency dropped ~30% within 30s, and allocator error rate decreased.

samir: while we do that, I'm kicking off compaction on the 10 affected hosts. script: `tools/arena/compact.sh --hosts host[101..110] --force` — will schedule briefly and should free fragmented slabs.

ops-bot: compaction job queued (job id cj-378888-01). ETA ~45s.

maria: good. we should also apply a short-term token-level throttle for heavy keys so a single long prefix doesn't expand cache. putting a temporary per-key cap 50MB.

ankit: applied per-key cap via feature-flag. monitoring.

jess: rolling the rollback + disable from canary to prod in waves. @kevin coordinate with deploy bot for rate-limited rollout.

kevin: initiating staggered rollout (2 hosts every 15s). logs showing fewer malloc errors as we roll.

incident-bot: Update: allocator error rate decreased 78% since canary rollback; latency P95 for embeddings down to 1.6x baseline (was 4x). Compaction job succeeded on 6/10 hosts, remaining 4 in progress.

maria: post-mortem hypothesis: a recent batcher tuning increased max_batch_tokens to handle long-context workloads. that increase allowed continuous batching to aggregate many prefixes into a single batch, causing rapid KV cache insert churn with many small allocations. The slab allocator couldn't compact because free segments were non-contiguous, leading to repeated `reslice` failures and eventual OOMs.

samir: mitigation checklist (short):
- revert batcher max_batch_tokens to previous stable value (done)
- disable continuous batching for embeddings route until allocator hotfix (partial)
- run arena compaction across affected fleet (in progress)
- enable per-key cache cap (done)
- add alert for slab_gap rate > 5/min (new)

ankit: medium-term: patch allocator to proactively coalesce small frees, and add a compaction trigger when prefix_cache growth rate > threshold. also evaluate bounding continuous batching by count as well as token budget.

jess: customer impact: started at 03:10, some embedding requests returned 5xx for ~8 minutes for a small subset of customers on the A/B test. CS notified.

maria: QA: need a test that simulates many small prefix inserts + large max_batch_tokens to reproduce locally. I'll own that.

kevin: engineering followups:
- KEVIN: open runtime PR with quick allocator pad/compaction (will target canary)
- MARIa: reproduce and add integration test
- ANKIT: alerts + rollout safe-guard for batcher config
- SAMIR: post-compaction verification script + runbook updates

jess: handing off to night oncall @maria. if any hosts still show `arena->reslice failed` after compaction, escalate to oncall-sre.

maria: taking handoff. current status summary: rollback + partial disable applied, compaction 60% done, per-key caps active, latency trending down. next check-in T+30m.

incident-bot: Incident acknowledged and assigned: incident-3788880000. Severity: Sev2 (customer impact, partial degradation).

jess: thanks team — please add timeline + raw logs to the incident doc and assign owners for the followups in the incident tracker.

kevin: added initial runbook notes to https://internal/incidents/3788880000/postmortem — will attach PR links once opened.

maria: note for postmortem: consider a config guard in the control plane preventing max_batch_tokens jumps > 2x without rollout freeze.

samir: adding compaction success markers to Fleet health dashboard.

maria: T+30m update: compaction complete on all hosts, allocator errors back to baseline, embedding route p95 at 1.1x baseline. Closing active mitigation; will keep monitoring and move to postmortem cadence.
